title: Gacha Girls Corps Anime Casts Ai Kayano, Rie Kugimiya
content:
The staff for the anime of author Chinkururi and illustrator Yasutaka Isegawa 's Gacha Girls Corps ( Gacha o Mawashite Nakama o Fuyasu: Saikyō no Bishōjo Gundan o Tsukuriagero ) light novel series announced two more cast members on Sunday.

Ai Kayano plays Shisuha Alvy, a UR-ranked priestess who is a healer but often goes berserk in battle.

Rie Kugimiya plays Luna Varedas, a UR-ranked vampire who is secretly a shut-in.

Kaiten Books describes the story:

UR-GUARANTEED—TO HAVE THE ADVENTURE OF A LIFETIME! Ready for an adventure that's out of this world? We've gacha covered. Norl's a cutting-edge cutie with a cutting edge who's a cut above the rest. Heihachi's just your average mobile game addict with a whale-sized hole in his wallet. But one day, he pulls an item that pulls him into another world, spinning his life around with a spin of the gacha. Attacked by monsters, and left without options, Heihachi does what he knows best—roll gacha! To his surprise, he watches his unit materialize before his eyes. Heihachi's used to seeing cute girls pop up on his phone, but he's never seen one pop out of his phone! Join him on his quest to collect OP UR QTs! (That's Overpowered Ultra Rare Cuties.)

The anime stars:

• Daisuke Sakaguchi as Heihachi Okura

• Miyu Tomita as Norl Fanya (name romanization not confirmed)

• Iori Noguchi as Estel

The anime's staff includes:

• Chief Director: Masahiro Takada

• Director: Takashi Asami

• Series Script Supervisor: Deko Akao

• Character Designer, Chief Animation Director: Miori Suzuki

• Monster Design: Tomoyuki Abe

• Prop Design Support: Shiori Kōno

• Art Director: Kenta Tsuboi

• Background Art: Minami Takizawa (name romanization not confirmed)

• Color Key Artist: Akiko Inoue

• Compositing Director of Photography: Kōsuke Tanaka

• Offline Editing: Masaki Utsunomiya

• Offline Editing Assistant: Asuka Kojima

• Sound Director: Nobuyuki Abe

• Sound Production: On-Lead

• Music: Hiroaki Tsutsumi, George King

• Music Producer: Takahiro Ikeda

• Background Music Production Collaboration: MIRACLE BUS

• Music Production: Starry Cube

• Animation Production: Zero-G× Saber Works

• Producer: Ryō Aizawa (Starry Cube)

• Executive Producer: Kōichirō Natsume

The anime will debut in January 2027.

Chinkururi launched the story on the Shōsetsuka ni Narō website in January 2016, and the series is ongoing. Micro Magazine published the ninth novel volume in August 2020.

Syū Haruno launched the manga adaptation on Comic Ride in 2018, and the 14th volume will ship on June 29.

Kaiten Books first licensed Haruno's manga adaptation in 2020. Omoi also digitally releases the manga in English. Kaiten Books released the manga's seventh volume digitally in September 2024.

Source s: Gacha Girls Corps anime's website , Comic Natalie

title: Bleach Just Made a Huge Change to Its Original Finale & Shocks With Big Death
content:
Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War has entered truly uncharted territory with its newest episode as it has made a huge change to how the manga’s final arc originally played out, and it’s shocked even further with a big death. Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War – The Calamity is now halfway through its run of final episodes for the long running anime franchise, and Ichigo Kurosaki is in the midst of his biggest fight in the series to date. And dealing with Yhwach has been much tougher than Ichigo ever could have prepared for.

While previous seasons of Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War made changes to Tite Kubo’s original Bleach manga to further flesh out its events , the newest episode of the anime has made some of the most significant changes to the story yet. Not only did Ichigo unlock a brand new Bankai form not seen in the original series, but this change ultimately resulted in the death of one of the franchise’s biggest characters, Orihime Inoue, as she made the ultimate sacrifice to save Ichigo from Yhwach.

Orihime Sacrifices Herself to Save Ichigo

Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War – The Calamity made a huge change to how this final fight between Ichigo and Yhwach originally played out in Tite Kubo’s original manga version of the events. In Episode 45, Ichigo is able to unleash his Bankai form that turns him into “Blood Chains Ichigo .” This is a completely new form created by Kubo himself, and was never seen in the manga. This change then completely alters how the rest of the episode goes as Yhwach is finally on the back foot for a while. But then he overwhelms Ichigo, and Orihime is pushed to her breaking point.

She had been brought to the fight to support Ichigo against Yhwach as her abilities to reject reality had been a major help against Yhwach’s Almighty power, and that was ultimately what helped saved Ichigo. Yhwach had killed both Orihime and Ichigo many times with all kinds of fatal blows, and only her abilities were enough to save them from the brink of death. But she makes the ultimate sacrifice towards the end of the episode as Yhwach tries to fully wipe out everyone.

Did Bleach Really Kill Off Orihime Before the Anime’s Finale?

Orihime then pushes her power beyond a level never seen before and is able to jump in front of Yhwach to save Ichigo one last time. The both of them are wiped out completely, and this seems to be the death of one of the series’ biggest characters. But that also can’t be the case considering how fans have known how Bleach really ends for ten years at this point . Orihime can’t be fully dead unless the creator is making a massive swerve that would take even long time fans by surprise.

In the original events of Bleach’ s final arc, this never happens as Ichigo never fully gets to reveal his new Bankai. Yhwach stops him before he was able to do so claiming that the Almighty power gave him the ability to see how big of a deal that form was in another kind of timeline, and that might end up happening here. This just might be a doomed timeline that will hopefully never come to pass. Or Orihime really has died. We’ll just have to see as Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War continues to air its final episodes with Hulu and Hulu on Disney+.

title: Netflix’s One Piece Season 3 Expands Alabasta With Major Cast Additions
content:
One Piece is hard at work on bringing its third season of the live-action series to Netflix next year, and it’s filling out more of its new cast with some major new additions. One Piece is gearing up to have a massive year in 2027 with more of the TV anime, a reboot series, a new feature film release and more on the way . But thankfully that also will feature the return of the live-action series as it gears up for its third season adapting the Straw Hats’ biggest fight yet.

Netflix’s One Piece live-action series will be kicking off its third season with the streaming service next year, and will be making its way to Alabasta after all of the set up for the arc in the second season. There are going to be many more faces making their way to the live-action series for this new region, and four new additions to the cast have been announced as part of the One Piece Day 2026 worldwide streaming event this past weekend with a huge update.

Netflix’s One Piece Season 3 Adds New Alabasta Characters

One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta has confirmed four new additions to the cast that the live-action series will be introducing once Luffy and the Straw Hats make landfall on the titular island . These include Emilio Sakraya ( Rheingold, Fortitude ) as Koza, Omid Abtahi ( The Mandalorian, American Gods ) as Toto, Jamie Ward ( The Gentlemen, His Dark Materials ) as Pell, and Nabeel Khan ( Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom, Strike Back ) as Chaka. Each of these faces will be a key recurring character in the new season too.

They join previously announced new additions for One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta such as Xolo Maridueña as Portgas D. Ace , Cole Escola as Bon Clay, Awdo Awdo as Mr. 1 and Daisy Head as Miss Doublefinger. It’s also been confirmed that Mikaela Hoover as Tony Tony Chopper, Charithra Chandran as Princess Vivi, Sendhil Ramamurthy as Nefartari Cobra, Lera Abova as Nico Robin, and Joe Manganiello as Sir Crocodile will be getting expanded roles in this third coming season too. It’s all going to be much bigger in this next season.

When Does Netflix’s One Piece Season 3 Come Out?

One Piece: The Battle of Alabasta is scheduled to make its debut with Netflix sometime in 2027 , but a more concrete release date has yet to be announced as of the time of this writing. The second season revealed that Vivi was a princess fleeing from the country in an attempt to figure out what’s going on with Baroque Works’ takeover, and Luffy and the others promised to help her once they made their way to the mysterious desert kingdom. It’s the biggest arc in the live-action series thus far.

It’s Luffy and the Straw Hats’ first major fight in the Grand Line, and all of the build up for Baroque Works seen across the first two seasons have been building to this. It’s yet to be revealed if the live-action series will be continuing beyond this point with more episodes, but this would be a perfect place to bring it all to an original end if that’s the route Netflix decides to go with it. We’ll just have to see how it all works out.

title: Comikey to Add Several Shōjo Manga from Hakusensha's Catalogue Digitally
content:
Comikey announced on August 17 it will release several shōjo manga titles from Hakusensha 's catalogue in English digitally. The first announced title is sora 's Crashout Schoolgirl and Degen Teacher ( Tsuiraku JK to Haijin Kyōshi ) and the first seven chapters are available to read now.

The company stated its lineup of Hakusensha titles will include manga that have not had official English releases before.

Comikey did not specifically state what other manga it will release from Hakusensha . The above image features the following manga (from left to right): Kōcha Ōji , Gakuen Babysitters , Tsuiraku JK to Haijin Kyōshi , Kare Kano , Moon Child , Ōkami-Heika no Hanayome , and Mikado no Shihō . Of these titles, Kare Kano and Moon Child have had English releases before.

The company previously partnered with Hakusensha to publish some of its titles in 2021.

Other new series that Comikey added in August include Kamiharu Haruno 's Shut Up, Takamori! ; Akinoko 's Learning to Love My Cat-like Classmate ; Asaki Asagiri and selen 's The Princess Groom ; and Nobuko Takekawa 's Yuko, the Ghost in My Room manga.

Comikey partnered with Shogakukan in July 2021, and began releasing titles in English digitally from the publisher. Comikey also publishes manga from Shinchosha , Compass, and Coamix .

Comikey users can read the first chapter and most recent chapter of each manga for free. For other chapters, users have the option to purchase the digital "Keys" currency to unlock those chapters.

Comikey was founded in 2020, and also hosts other Asian comics such as webtoons and manhua. The company also localizes series into Portuguese. The platform officially launched in June 2021 with content from KuaiKan Manhua.

title: 37 Years Later, Legendary Sports Series Is Getting Its First-Ever U.S. Release
content:
Sports anime such as Haikyu and Blue Lock have been on the rise in recent years, but several classics came before them to pave the path for the genre’s success. Fans often love the underdog trope in sports series where the protagonist, who everyone underestimates, gets to shine due to his grit and dedication. One such manga is the classic boxing series, Hajime no Ippo , written and illustrated by George Morikawa. The manga began serialization in Kodansha’s Weekly Shonen Magazine in 1989. The series has won several awards over the decades, including the 15th Kodansha Manga Award in the Shounen category in 1991. Not only that, but this beloved manga made history in 2023 when it crossed the 100 million milestone.

Only 24 manga in history have achieved this level of popularity, which makes Hajime no Ippo all the more special . However, despite its historic success, the manga was never officially released in the U.S. 37 years after its debut, the official website of Kodansha confirmed that the manga will get its English print starting next year. The announcement was shared during Kodansha’s Anime NYC panel on August 21st, 2026. While the English adaptation of the manga has officially been confirmed for Fall 2027, the exact release date will be announced at a later date.

Hajime no Ippo Continues Its Indefinite Hiatus

The manga went on an indefinite hiatus in December last year due to the creator’s poor health. Morikawa underwent abdominal surgery last year, which is why he plans to take a long break before returning with the weekly series. Even though several months have passed since the manga went on a break, there are currently no plans for it to resume serialization.

Hajime no Ippo has been ongoing for several decades, and it might end not long after its return. The creator already confirmed in 2023 that he has planned the series’ ending, but didn’t reveal when he plans to conclude it. While fans await updates on the manga’s return, the anime’s future looks even more bleak.

Will Hajime no Ippo Return With a New Anime Season?

More than a decade after the manga began serialization, Madhouse adapted this epic story in 2000 . Since then, the anime has released several seasons and OVA episodes, some of which were released under the banner of both Madhouse and Studio MAPPA. However, the anime hasn’t returned since 2014, and the animation studio has no plans on prioritizing this legendary series. Even with the hiatus, the manga has more than enough material left to adapt at least a few seasons, but due to the change in trends in the industry, studios often prefer shorter series instead of long-running stories that have been ongoing for decades.

Madhouse is one of the oldest studios in the country, but it has recently focused on global hits such as Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End , which is currently the highest-rated fantasy series. While Hajime no Ippo still maintains a dedicated fanbase, the anime may not be the best medium to enjoy the story to the fullest. This is why the latest update from Kodansha is a major win for fans outside of Japan.

title: One Piece Confirms 2 New Movies & Is Making History With Biggest Arc Yet
content:
One Piece has officially announced that it’s now working on two new feature film releases for the near future, and the first of these movies is making history for the franchise when it adapts one of the biggest events in Eiichiro Oda’s original manga yet. It’s been no secret that One Piece has been hard at work on a new feature film release for quite a while as Oda himself confirmed this to be the case not long ago, but there was an even bigger surprise for fans in store.

One Piece took the stage during a special worldwide streamed One Piece Day 2026 event this past weekend and revealed some big updates for the franchise’s future. It was here that Toei Animation confirmed that they were not only working on a new One Piece movie, but revealed that their are actually two new movies now in the works. But the first of these movies is going against a major trend for the franchise as it’s actually set to adapt materials from Oda’s manga with the God Valley flashback. Check out the announcement trailer below.

One Piece Announces New Movies for 2027 and 2029

One Piece Film God Valley has been announced for a scheduled release in Japan sometime in Summer 2027, and then it will be followed by One Piece Film BAAD coming in 2029. International release dates or plans have yet to be revealed as of the time of this initial announcement, nor has it yet to be confirmed what production staff is going to bring these new movies to life. But there’s quite a lot to dig into with the announcement of these new movies given they buck a big trend.

One Piece Film God Valley will be adapting the God Valley flashback arc as seen during the events of the Elbaph arc of Eiichiro Oda’s original manga series. This does make a lot of sense given that the God Valley incident doesn’t take up many chapters of the manga release, and could be told within a single movie’s runtime. But that does raise a lot of questions about how the TV anime is going to move forward since the film is the first in this long running franchise to directly adapt the manga’s story.

What Does This Mean for One Piece’s TV Anime Future?

The first phase of One Piece: Elbaph Arc will be ending its run in just a few more weeks with the end of the Summer 2026 anime schedule , and then the TV anime will be taking a few months off before returning with its next season in 2027. The TV series has confirmed it will only be releasing 26 episodes a year overall, so there’s a chance that it might be using this movie to fully adapt the God Valley incident and thus skipping over it in the episodes themselves. Which is certainly going to be interesting when thinking about its worldwide audience.

If One Piece Film God Valley indeed covers the God Valley flashback next Summer , right when it would take place in the TV anime’s version of the Elbaph Arc, then there’s a chance that fans outside of Japan will be missing this crucial piece of context as the TV anime continues the story beyond the incident. Since this seems to be the first movie with a not-original story, fans are going to want to keep a close eye on this one to see what’s next.

One Piece took the stage during a special worldwide streamed One Piece Day 2026 event this past weekend and revealed some big updates for the franchise’s future. It was here that Toei Animation confirmed that they were not only working on a new One Piece movie, but revealed that their are actually two new movies now in the works. But the first of these movies is going against a major trend for the franchise as it’s actually set to adapt materials from Oda’s manga with the God Valley flashback. Check out the announcement trailer below.
One Piece Announces New Movies for 2027 and 2029

One Piece Film God Valley has been announced for a scheduled release in Japan sometime in Summer 2027, and then it will be followed by One Piece Film BAAD coming in 2029. International release dates or plans have yet to be revealed as of the time of this initial announcement, nor has it yet to be confirmed what production staff is going to bring these new movies to life. But there’s quite a lot to dig into with the announcement of these new movies given they buck a big trend.

One Piece Film God Valley will be adapting the God Valley flashback arc as seen during the events of the Elbaph arc of Eiichiro Oda’s original manga series. This does make a lot of sense given that the God Valley incident doesn’t take up many chapters of the manga release, and could be told within a single movie’s runtime. But that does raise a lot of questions about how the TV anime is going to move forward since the film is the first in this long running franchise to directly adapt the manga’s story.
What Does This Mean for One Piece’s TV Anime Future?

The first phase of One Piece: Elbaph Arc will be ending its run in just a few more weeks with the end of the Summer 2026 anime schedule , and then the TV anime will be taking a few months off before returning with its next season in 2027. The TV series has confirmed it will only be releasing 26 episodes a year overall, so there’s a chance that it might be using this movie to fully adapt the God Valley incident and thus skipping over it in the episodes themselves. Which is certainly going to be interesting when thinking about its worldwide audience.

If One Piece Film God Valley indeed covers the God Valley flashback next Summer , right when it would take place in the TV anime’s version of the Elbaph Arc, then there’s a chance that fans outside of Japan will be missing this crucial piece of context as the TV anime continues the story beyond the incident. Since this seems to be the first movie with a not-original story, fans are going to want to keep a close eye on this one to see what’s next.

title: BLEACH: Thousand-Year Blood War Reveals Creditless Ending Scene Video From Episode 5
content:
BLEACH: Thousand-Year Blood War (TYBW) Part 4 revealed the non-credit ending video from Episode 5 “DEFEND YOU.” The anime previously revealed Ichigo’s new Blood Chains form that was also introduced in the episode, which was mostly anime-original. The anime returned with the fourth and final cour, subtitled The Calamity , on July 25. It is set to run for a total 10 episodes.

The new video features the ending song “Rasen” by 9Lana and features Orihime Inoue’s scene from the end of the latest episode. You can watch the video below.

ALSO READ: BLEACH JET Artbook and Ryogo Narita’s School Life Novel Return, Fan Vote and 2027 Exhibition Announced

Created by Tite Kubo, BLEACH was serialized in Weekly Shonen Jump from 2001 to 2016 and concluded with 74 volumes. The manga has exceeded 130 million copies in circulation worldwide, making it one of the best-selling manga series of all time.

The original anime adaptation aired from 2004 to 2012 and received four theatrical films. The franchise returned in 2022 with BLEACH: Thousand-Year Blood War , adapting the manga’s final arc. Its final part (Part 4) is set to release in July. Tite Kubo has confirmed it will include even more original material than the previous parts , expanding the manga’s final battles.

On a related note, BLEACH: Mirrors High revealed its protagonists in a new trailer, with the game featuring original character designs by Tite Kubo.

title: Midori Amagaeru, Tsukasa Kyoka's 'Online - The Comic' Manga Ends
content:
Manga Box published the 255th and final chapter of Midori Amagaeru and Tsukasa Kyoka 's Online: The Comic manga on August 14. Amagaeru shared an illustration celebrating the end of the manga.

The manga launched on DeNA 's MangaBox app in 2013. The English version of the app, which also launched in 2013, also published the manga digitally in English, until MangaBox discontinued its English app. MangaBox describes the story:

Mai Yashiro (22) was an average office worker until the day a video game console arrived in her mailbox. The game she is forced to play, “Nightmare,” is a dangerous game in which one risks both the lives of the ones they love and their own body!! If you refuse to play, those dear to you die. If you lose battles in the game, parts of your body (your arms or legs, your voice, etc.) cease functioning. The horror of this game spreads throughout society in a flash, and, to fight it, Mai's company creates a “Nightmare” Strategy Team. After being assigned to this team, Mai and her dependable comrades boldly rise up against this hellish game. Adapted from the super-popular novel which has received over 40,000,000 hits online!!

Everystar shipped the 23rd compiled book volume on February 1. Amazon previously listed in 2020 the series as ending with the 15th volume.

Amagaeru launched the original novel series in 2011, and Kadokawa published the 27th novel in May 2024.

title: 1 Year Later, Crunchyroll Is Finally Streaming Solo Leveling’s Breakout Replacement
content:
Solo Leveling confirmed an anime sequel in July this year, more than a year after the second season finale. The series’ first feature-length film will follow the story after the fan-favorite Jeju Island Arc. However, the anime has yet to confirm a release window. While fans await Solo Leveling ‘s return, Crunchyroll began streaming just the perfect series for fans. Super Cube is a donghua that went viral last year thanks to its spectacular animation. In recent years, the Chinese animation industry has been on the rise thanks to unique stories and unique animation style. The fight choreography especially captured viewers’ eyes, even more than the story itself.

Crunchyroll often streams such series, including the beloved mystery drama Link Click and the popular isekai Lord of Mysteries . While Super Cube premiered in 2025, the platform wasn’t streaming it until now. The series is also available on Prime Video through the Crunchyroll Amazon Channel add-on. While Crunchyroll hasn’t made an official announcement yet, you can find all episodes of the first season on the website. The series debuted on Crunchyroll on August 21st, 2026, as fans await updates on the second season.

Will Super Cube Release a Season 2?

Although there are rumors circulating around the second season, the animation studio and the producers have yet to officially confirm it. Considering the popularity of the donghua, it wouldn’t be surprising if we get an official announcement soon. Now that Crunchyroll has also licensed the show, the chances of a sequel season have only skyrocketed. The donghua is based on a Chinese webtoon with over 300 chapters, so there’s a lot of story left to adapt.

The series centers around Wang Xiaoxiu, who has been in love with his childhood friend, Shen Yao, for as long as he can remember. After they both enrolled in college, she accepts his feelings for her, but that was only the beginning of his struggles. Xiaoxiu finds himself being targeted by a group of delinquents led by Sun Jun, who also wants to pursue Yao. After they threw Xiaoxiu into the river, the ordinary college student finds a mysterious cube that merges with his body and grants him unique powers. The second season will continue his journey as he combats the threats around him with the help of his newfound abilities.

How Is Super Cube Similar to Solo Leveling ?

While both series are different at their cores, they do have the same narrative structure. Both series follow the underdog protagonists who gain extraordinary powers after a near-death situation. Not to mention that even the dark-haired appearance of both protagonists is somewhat similar. While Xiaoxiu’s main power is teleportation, it is also an ability Jinwoo is capable of using.

After Xiaoxiu gained his new powers, he does everything he can to become good at fighting, which is pretty much the same thing Jinwoo had going for him . However, despite the similarities, both series have completely different power systems and overall world-building.

title: 'Gacha wo Mawashite Nakama wo Fuyasu' Announces Additional Cast Pair
content:
The official website for the television anime adaptation of Chinkururi and Nanashina 's Gacha wo Mawashite Nakama wo Fuyasu: Saikyou no Bishoujo Gundan wo Tsukuriagero ( Gacha Girls Corps ) light novel announced a pair of additional cast on Sunday. The anime series will premiere in January 2027.

Voice actresses Ai Kayano ( Kono Subarashii Sekai ni Shukufuku wo! ) and Rie Kugimiya ( Gintama ) are joining the cast as Shisuha Aibi and Luna Varad, respectively.

Takashi Asami ( Ginga Eiyuu Densetsu episode director) is helming the anime at Zero-G and Saber Works . Deko Akao ( Norigami Arigato ) is handling the series composition. Mineo Suzuki ( Konyaku Haki sareta Reijou wo Hirotta Ore ga, Ikenai Koto wo Oshiekomu ) is designing the characters and serving as the chief animation director. Hiroaki Tsutsumi ( Jujutsu Kaisen ) and George King are composing the music.

Chinkururi originally published the fantasy adventure novel with illustrations by Nanashina as a web novel on the Shousetsuka ni Narou website in January 2016. Micro Magazine published the nine volumes under the GC Novels imprint between November 2016 and August 2020 featuring illustrations by Nanashina.

Comic Ride began serializing a manga adaptation by Shuu Haruno in March 2018. The 14th volume was released on June 29.

Kaiten Books licensed the manga adaptation in English in December 2020 and released the seventh volume digitally in September 2024.
